entries.note: Two things live in the per-launch context and they have opposite rules. The BINDING -- url, token, instance, rootId -- is taken once from the facade's snapshot (RENGINE_MCP_CONTEXT_SNAPSHOT) precisely so that editing the file cannot retarget a running CLI to another project (spec 065); do not make the binding follow the file. The IDENTITY is the conversation, and the conversation can legitimately change under a running CLI: report-session.mjs rewrites this file when Claude Code's SessionStart hook says the process moved to another session id. So the identity alone is re-read, once per tool call at the top of scopedState, and identityHeaders is a function rather than a frozen object -- a frozen object passes workspace_info and still puts the stale id on the wire, which is the ledger's whole input. A missing, torn or anonymous file leaves the identity as it was rather than dropping it.

KI-110. This arm used to be `let Some(directory) = ... else { return host }`: a context without the field routed the pane to the SESSION HOST, which declares eight capabilities fewer than the root-bound worker. Spec 095 names the computed directory as the fallback 'an older supervisor leaves', and runtime/discovery.mjs has always defaulted to it, so returning the host contradicted both. The default is <checkout>/.cache/runtime/<instance>, the same path runtimeDirectory(host) produces. The checkout comes from the BINARY (current_exe, four ancestors up) rather than CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, because CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR is baked at compile time while the JS resolves its own module URL -- it names the checkout the code is RUNNING from, which is what a sibling checkout's workspace needs. That is red-project's existing choice for its built surface adapter (games.rs adapter_path), and it is why checkout_of is a pure function on a path: the hop count is the fragile part and it is pinned by a test of its own, separate from the resolution test, which cannot see a wrong hop because it computes the same one. A binary named by RENGINE_RED_MCP from outside its own checkout is the residual case; it resolves against wherever that binary lives, as every other red-* crate does.
